events.summary: Calnex Solutions Plc (LSE: CLX, Edinburgh) said it is expanding its existing partnership with VIAVI. Calnex's network emulators (SNE, SNE-X, SNE-Ignite) will be combined with VIAVI's lab test products (ONE LabPro, TestCenter, CyberFlood) so customers can test networks and applications under realistic traffic and network faults. The release names AI infrastructure, data center, defense, satcom, enterprise and Open RAN as use cases. The two companies already worked together on Open RAN testing (VIAVI TM500, TeraVM, XEdge with Calnex Paragon-neo, SNE-Ignite, SNE-X). The release gives no financial terms, no customer names and no exclusivity. It is quoted by Mark Bateman, VIAVI Vice President, Sales and Channel, Lab and Production, and Graeme Urquhart, VP Sales at Calnex. The release was issued by Calnex; it did not appear on VIAVI's own investor-relations press-release feed (checked 2026-10-07 22:09 UTC). Timestamp: Yahoo shows 4:00 PM GMT+2 (14:00 UTC, 10:00 ET); the PR Newswire UK page shows 15:36 GMT. Either way it came out during the US session.
events.why_it_matters: It is a sales-channel and technical tie-up for VIAVI's lab test products, including the AI data-center use case, but there are no money terms, so it is unlikely to change revenue expectations. The stock fell on the day it came out, so it did not drive the move.

products.name: VIAVI lab test products in the Calnex tie-up (ONE LabPro, TestCenter, CyberFlood), paired with Calnex SNE network emulators
products.what_it_is: VIAVI's products generate realistic network traffic and simulate users. Calnex's emulators recreate the faults of real networks (delays, lost data, distance). Together they let engineers test a network or application in the lab under real-world conditions before it goes live.
products.analogy: VIAVI supplies the test cars and crash-test dummies; Calnex builds the bumpy, foggy test track. Together they show how the network copes before real customers drive on it.
products.buyers: Per the release: AI infrastructure, data center, defense, satcom, enterprise and Open RAN users. No customer names were disclosed.
products.how_it_works: A traffic generator (for example TestCenter, or CyberFlood for application and security traffic) sends line-rate or application-level traffic through the system under test. A network emulator (Calnex SNE) sits in the path and adds controlled impairments (latency, packet loss, jitter), and the tester measures how performance holds up. TestCenter and CyberFlood were Spirent product lines before VIAVI acquired Spirent (general knowledge, not re-verified this run).
products.sales: not disclosed for these products or for the partnership. Proxy (labelled): VIAVI's NSE network-test segment had Q4 FY2026 revenue of $353.9M (+69.2%), and management said the data-center ecosystem is about 50% of NSE.
products.sales_source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000912093/000162828026053381/viavq4fy268-kex991.htm (2026-08-05, segment revenue); https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/viavi-solutions-inc-viav-q4-051054244.html (2026-08-06, ~50% data-center share, call highlights, tier 3)
products.stage: Both companies' products are shipping. The partnership extends an existing Open RAN collaboration to AI/data-center, defense, satcom and enterprise use cases. No contract value was given. VIAVI added a smaller CyberFlood CF50 platform on 2026-09-29 (VIAVI IR feed).
products.size_for_company: not disclosed. Probably small next to $443.1M of quarterly revenue, because it is a technical/channel tie-up with no stated financial terms (inference, medium).
products.competition: Keysight Technologies is VIAVI's main test-and-measurement rival (general knowledge, not sourced this run). Competing emulator vendors were not checked.
products.why_investors_care: It shows VIAVI's Spirent-derived lab products being bundled into AI-infrastructure test setups through partners. That is mildly supportive of the data-center testing thesis, but there are no numbers.
products.watch_next: Whether VIAVI mentions joint customer wins or partner-driven sales on the Q1 FY2027 call, and the data-center share of NSE revenue.
